claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has a conventional alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure in the as-received state.
Cold-spray deposition of a RHEA coating followed by low-temperature heat treatment will form a graded diffusion layer at the coating–substrate interface.
The graded diffusion layer will enhance hardness relative to untreated TC4.
The graded diffusion layer will improve wear resistance under high-contact-stress conditions relative to untreated TC4.
The coating and heat-treatment intervention will preserve TC4's intrinsic alpha-plus-beta microstructure.
Low-temperature heat treatment can promote interfacial diffusion without causing deleterious phase transformations when kept below critical temperatures.
A graded diffusion layer strengthens interfacial bonding.
A graded diffusion layer prevents the formation of brittle intermetallic compounds.
Cold spraying deposits the coating with minimal thermal input.
The minimal thermal input of cold spraying avoids unwanted phase transformations.
Subsequent low-temperature heat treatment facilitates limited atomic interdiffusion at the coating–substrate interface.
Limited interfacial interdiffusion produces a robust, graded bond.
The robust graded bond effectively transfers stress across the coating–substrate interface.
The intervention will preserve ductility relative to untreated TC4.
The intervention will preserve microstructural integrity relative to untreated TC4.
Untreated TC4 has poor friction and wear resistance under high-contact conditions.
Temperatures above the proposed processing window may induce harmful intermetallic formation or significant microstructural alterations.
